approval_boundary: Static illustrated evidence only. No native model, motion, collision, automation, inventory or runtime approval.
scope: Full four-panel N02 expanded network candidate, including timber and mineral house routes, self-service destinations and both industrial views.

defects.repair: Connect each incoming lane to the receiving roller module; keep the separate cash pad and front service apron.

defects.finding: The saw output lane ends against the house side beside the front-facing IN aperture. The actual dark IN mouth remains visibly uncoupled.
defects.repair: Add a supported bend into the existing mouth, or rotate the whole house to expose the protected utility wall and connect the true input.

defects.finding: The iron lane meets the bench left upright/wood edge beside the front roller nip. It does not visibly reach the approved rear-left iron receiving rack.
defects.repair: Reposition the bench or route the lane behind the rollers into the existing rear-left receiving rack, with a visible supported bridge. Preserve manual sheet pickup and clear controls.

defects.finding: The BLOCK OUT label and solid side plate obscure the dark outlet mouth at the join, weakening the traceability established by approved detail22.
defects.repair: Expose the same dark OUT aperture above the roller bridge, with the label above it.

positive_findings: The mineral house IN already has a legible bend into its actual mouth.
Compact planks, blocks, iron and cash remain comfortable relative to C1.
Timber and mineral modes are separate typed studies; finished industrial sheets remain manual pickup with no industrial sales counter.
Machine identities and front worker aisles remain legible.
matrix_boundary: The existing focused industrial inset satisfies the matrix camera category; no new opposing-camera requirement is introduced. Physical interfaces still must be traceable.
